description: This project appears to be a decentralized finance (DeFi) protocol centered around a custom automated market maker (AMM) called 'Seawater', integrated with a loyalty/rewards system (Leo) and a faucet for token distribution. It implements liquidity pools, token swaps, position management via NFTs, and campaign-based reward mechanisms, with a test suite and a Rust-based Stylus smart contract component for on-chain execution.

contracts.name: SeawaterAMM
contracts.purpose: Core AMM contract implementing liquidity pool management, token swaps, and position operations. Likely an upgradeable proxy pattern given storage slot constants.
state_variables: Storage slots defined via keccak (e.g., E, etc.)

contracts.name: OwnershipNFTs
contracts.purpose: ERC721 NFT contract for tracking ownership of positions in the Seawater AMM, enabling liquidity providers to manage and transfer their positions.

contracts.name: Faucet
contracts.purpose: Distributes ERC20 tokens to specified recipients, possibly for testing or rewards, with operator controls and random amount selection.

contracts.name: ISeawaterAMM
contracts.purpose: Public-facing interface for the Seawater AMM, combining event definitions and executor swap interfaces for comprehensive interaction.

contracts.name: ISeawaterExecutorSwap
contracts.purpose: Defines the interface for swap operations within a pool, specifying parameters for token swaps and fee handling.

contracts.name: ISeawaterEvents
contracts.purpose: Defines event emissions for the Seawater AMM, such as position minting, burning, fee collection, and swaps.

contracts.name: ILeoEvents
contracts.purpose: Defines events for the Leo rewards system, including campaign balance updates, creation, and transfers.

contracts.name: ISeawaterMigrations
contracts.purpose: Empty interface for potential future migration functions in the Seawater protocol.

contracts.name: IERC721TokenReceiver
contracts.purpose: Standard interface for receiving ERC721 tokens, used by contracts that need to accept NFT transfers.

contracts.name: IERC721Metadata
contracts.purpose: Standard interface for ERC721 metadata (name, symbol, tokenURI), used by OwnershipNFTs.

contracts.name: IERC20
contracts.purpose: Standard ERC20 interface for token interactions, used across the project.

contracts.name: IFaucet
contracts.purpose: Interface for the Faucet contract, defining struct for distribution requests and external functions.

contracts.name: LightweightERC20
contracts.purpose: A gas-efficient ERC20 implementation with EIP-2612 permit support, likely used for testing or as a base token in the protocol.

contracts.name: Permit2
contracts.purpose: Uniswap's Permit2 contract for signature-based token transfers, integrated for gasless approvals.

contracts.name: libleo (Rust)
contracts.purpose: Rust library implementing interactions with the Seawater AMM, likely for campaign rewards or calculations, compiled to WASM for Stylus.

contracts.name: libleo (main)
contracts.purpose: Entry point for the Leo Stylus contract, handling user entrypoint and compiling to WASM.

contracts.name: libleo (maths)
contracts.purpose: Mathematical utilities (e.g., mul-div) used in Leo contract calculations.

contracts.name: libleo (immutables)
contracts.purpose: Defines immutable values like contract addresses for the Leo system, with test-only dummy values.

relationships.description: SeawaterAMM implements the ISeawaterAMM interface for public functions and events.
SeawaterAMM imports and uses executor swap interfaces for internal swap logic.
SeawaterAMM interacts with OwnershipNFTs to mint/burn NFTs representing positions.
OwnershipNFTs calls back into SeawaterAMM for position validation or updates.
Faucet transfers ERC20 tokens using the IERC20 interface.
Faucet implements the IFaucet interface for distribution functions.
ISeawaterAMM imports event definitions from ISeawaterEvents.
libleo interacts with SeawaterAMM via raw calls for reward collection or calculations.
libleo main uses the seawater module for core logic.
OwnershipNFTs implements the receiver interface to handle NFT transfers.
OwnershipNFTs implements metadata functions for NFTs.
LightweightERC20 implements the IERC20 interface for token operations.
Permit2 uses EIP-712 for domain separation in signatures.

high_risk_areas.reason: Storage slot constants suggest a proxy pattern; incorrect storage layout or upgrades could lead to data corruption or vulnerabilities.
Complex callbacks and state synchronization between AMM and NFT contracts may introduce reentrancy or inconsistency risks.
Direct ERC20 transfers without checks for balance or approval could lead to failed transactions or exploitation if not carefully controlled.
Raw calls to external contracts (e.g., SeawaterAMM) from Rust/WASM may lack proper validation or error handling, risking reentrancy or unexpected behavior.
Custom math functions like mul-div must be secure against overflow/underflow; errors could affect reward calculations or pool balances.
NFT minting/burning in OwnershipNFTs must align with AMM state; mismatches could lead to orphaned positions or theft.
